justification: Changes the production DCP change monitor: which files are downloaded each run, what is recorded, and what the daily alarm calls red. A wrong cadence decision silently skips a changed file; a wrong alarm query stays green over an unchecked chapter. Adds a migration (3 tables, 1 column).

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-10-22 read-only on production: no dcp_monitor_* tables and no url_last_downloaded column; 571 active chapters, 541 with a council_url, 454 tagged (ETag), 544 with a council_page_url across 21 councils. Unwatched: inner_west 495 served provisions (no registry row), nsw_statewide 31 setbacks. 28 auto_detected new documents waiting since 2026-05-18 across 5 councils. 6 chapters with needs_extraction.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: (1) v6 said drop query strings when normalising links; canada_bay and liverpool name the document in the query, so only cache-buster keys are dropped. (2) The #1430 chapter-number match never fires on Bayside: its new edition is titled with the whole plan name and no part number, so a whole-plan name+year match was added. (3) v6 implied a new alert table; new hub documents are already registered as auto_detected registry rows and that row is reused as the review item and dedupe state. (4) The old monitor already executes UPDATEs in --dry-run (it only skips commit).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Nothing changes until migration 116 is applied and dcp-monitor is deployed from main. The cron stays fortnightly in this PR; the daily cron is a separate PR after the deploy (the drift check compares the file with the live value, and old code must not run daily).
pre_impl.external_source_error: Council hub pages and document servers fail in four ways that are each recorded, never dropped: HubScrapeError 403 -> council outcome 'blocked', other hub errors -> 'error', an empty scrape -> 'empty', fewer than 80% of expected links -> 'anomaly'; per chapter 403 -> waf_blocked, 429 twice -> rate_limited, timeouts -> transient, anything else -> failed. A gone link whose HEAD cannot be read is reported as 'file not checked', never as removed.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend change. The new tables are read only by scripts/verifyops_coverage.py and by people; no API route or component reads them in this PR (the site banner is a later step).
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If this is wrong a site visitor is shown a DCP chapter as current when the council changed it: a cadence bug that skips a download, or an alarm query that stays green over an unchecked chapter. Both fail silently, which is why every outcome is stored and the alarm is red on anything it cannot read (exit 2).

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest -q tests/test_verifyops_daily_check.py tests/test_r2_monitor_alerting.py tests/test_hub_discovery_is_not_gated_on_change_detection.py tests/test_dockerfile_monitors_imports.py ; PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 DATABASE_URL=<pooler url> python -m pytest -m database -o addopts= tests/test_verifyops_coverage_real_db.py tests/test_verifyops_record_real_db.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: an untagged file is downloaded before 7 days or not at 7, a tag change or spot check does not download, the spot check picks more than once a week, the shadow week is not exactly 7 days, a dry run writes, a rate-limited skip is not recorded, a re-upload or chapter number is misread, a redesign hides a held-chapter match, a delisted file is called gone, a plan without a year matches, the alarm lets a new key cancel a cleared one, cannot-look reads as a pass, or --update raises the baseline
falsifiable_check.observed_red: YES: 35 hand-made mutants applied one at a time to verifyops_record/links/coverage. 33 killed. 1 equivalent (flush without the dry_run guard: a dry run never gets a run_id). The SQL survivor is now killed by the real-database tests (TEMP copies of the migration-116 tables on production, rolled back): 5 SQL mutants, 5 killed - last.outcome NOT IN -> IN, the ok filter on list_not_read_2d dropped, the checked-outcome filter on not_checked_8d dropped, two INSERT columns swapped, and the ok filter on the previous-list lookup dropped (that one first SURVIVED and got its own test: a blocked day's empty list must never become the list compared with). Two real bugs were found by the tests before commit: dcp_part_3.pdf read as a re-upload of dcp_part.pdf, and 'exhibitions' not flagged as draft. A third by the real canada_bay list: 3 new links on an 8-link page read as a redesign (floor of 5 added).

functions.name: decide_fetch
functions.input: stored hash/tag/size, HEAD tag/size, last full download, now, spot flag
functions.output: a pair (download today?, reason) where reason is one of force, no_baseline, etag_changed, spot_check, etag_match, size_changed, untagged_weekly, untagged_recent
functions.if_none: no stored hash or no last download -> download

functions.name: is_spot_check
functions.input: the registry chapter id (int) and the run time (timezone-aware datetime, UTC)
functions.output: bool, ~1 in 20 per ISO week, one weekday
functions.if_none: not applicable: both arguments are always present; the pick is pure arithmetic on them, so the same chapter and week always give the same answer

functions.name: council_list_checked
functions.input: one council's slug, hub URL, the scraper's discovered list of {chapter_key,url,label}, held chapter labels, plan names, a probe and a sender
functions.output: saved list + alert lines; Telegram only after the shadow week
functions.if_none: an empty scrape is stored as outcome 'empty' with no diff, so the alarm sees the council as not read rather than unchanged

functions.name: diff_lists
functions.input: the last list stored with outcome 'ok' for this council (or None) and today's normalised link entries
functions.if_none: no previous list means a first scan: today's list is saved and no alert is raised, the setup run never alerts

functions.name: main
functions.input: argv flags --update and --allow-raise, plus DATABASE_URL from the environment or an injected connection for tests
functions.if_none: a missing DATABASE_URL or a missing dcp_monitor table exits 2, which dq_check reports as unverifiable and the workflow step as failed, never 0

queries.purpose: record each run / council list / chapter outcome
last good list for a council
queries.where_clause: council = %s AND outcome = 'ok' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1
active AND NOT inert chapters; per reason windows 2/8/30/3/33 days

break_it.scenario: A server keeps the ETag but changes the bytes
break_it.what_happens: caught only on the weekly 1-in-20 spot download
break_it.how: outcome etag_lied -> red key for 30 days; stated residual risk in the spec

break_it.scenario: A chapter's server answers HTTP 429 to the HEAD request twice in a row
break_it.what_happens: recorded rate_limited, listed in the run summary and Telegram infra note, red key last_run_unchecked

break_it.scenario: Council page redesigned; one new link is the new edition of a held chapter
break_it.what_happens: one redesign line plus the matching link's own line

break_it.scenario: The new code is deployed to Railway before migration 116 is applied to the database
break_it.what_happens: dcp-monitor fails at its first SELECT (url_last_downloaded) and exits 1; check_railway_jobs_ran goes red

break_it.scenario: The daily alarm runs before any monitor run has recorded results in the new tables
break_it.what_happens: exit 2 (could not look) or every chapter red
break_it.how: baseline written from the first real run with --update --allow-raise

break_it.scenario: One of the alarm's red keys queries returns no rows because its predicate is wrong, so an unchecked chapter is not reported
break_it.what_happens: the alarm stays green over the gap - the one silent mode left in this PR
break_it.how: unit tests pin every window and table; the predicate meaning is checked on the first live run by reading each red key against the registry and confirming a known-unchecked chapter (camden, no council_url) appears as no_url

verification_after_merge: 1. Apply migrations/116_dcp_monitor_results.sql (user go). VERIFY: 3 dcp_monitor_* tables.
2. Deploy dcp-monitor from main once Railway Hobby deploys resume; trigger one run.
3. Separate PR: cron 0 2 * * * + live value + DQ-117 window + tests/test_one_outcome_alarm.py. The alarm's 2-day windows assume it.
4. After the first DAILY run: count chapter results per outcome for that run_id (one terminal row per active chapter), run python scripts/verifyops_coverage.py and read every red key.
5. python scripts/verifyops_coverage.py --update --allow-raise 'first daily run <date>'. Never before step 3, or the alarm is red for most of each fortnight.

post_merge.db_reset: Apply migrations/116_dcp_monitor_results.sql once to production (additive: 3 new tables, 1 nullable column; rollback in the file header). Needs the user's go.
post_merge.secrets: None added. The GitHub DATABASE_URL secret predates the 2026-10-22 password rotation and must be updated for freshness-alarm (and this new step) to log in; RAILWAY_TOKEN likely needs replacing too, as Railway voided all API tokens at 04:17 UTC that day.
post_merge.other_repo: None. Railway: dcp-monitor must be deployed from main after merge (deploys are paused for Hobby workspaces as of 2026-10-22).
post_merge.manual_verify: After the daily cron is live and its first run has recorded results: count chapter results per outcome for that run_id (one terminal row per active chapter), run python scripts/verifyops_coverage.py and read every red key, then write the baseline with --update --allow-raise 'first daily run <date>'.
